deepseek_v4_pro/001: The strategy for this policy is to use a minimax search with alpha-beta pruning, evaluating positions based on mobility (number of available moves), corner control, and disc stability. The search depth adapts based on remaining empty squares to stay within time limits. In the early game, it prioritizes mobility and corner proximity; in the late game, it maximizes disc count.
deepseek_v4_pro/002: The strategy for this policy is an iterative deepening alpha-beta search with a time limit of 0.9 seconds. The evaluation function uses a weighted combination of positional weights (corner, edge, and X-square heuristics), mobility (number of legal moves), and disc count. The weights are dynamically adjusted based on the game stage (early, mid, late). Move ordering is done by evaluating the resulting board with a quick positional score, prioritizing corners. The search correctly handles passes and terminal states.
deepseek_v4_pro/003: The strategy for this policy is based on an efficient bitboard representation of the Othello board. It uses iterative deepening alpha-beta search with a static evaluation function. The evaluation function combines a weighted board matrix (favoring corners and penalizing C/X-squares) with a piece differential in the endgame. Moves are ordered by the static evaluation of resulting positions to maximize pruning. The search depth is limited by a 0.95-second time budget per move, allowing it to adapt to the hardware.
deepseek_v4_pro/004: The strategy uses a high-performance bitboard-based Othello engine with iterative deepening negamax search and alpha-beta pruning. The evaluation function incorporates corner dominance, penalizes risky X/C-squares when corners are empty, rewards edge control, mobility advantage in the early and midgame, disc count in the endgame, and a parity bonus for the last move. Move ordering uses static positional weights to prioritize corners and edges, with the best move from the previous iteration searched first. Time management caps thinking at 0.95 seconds to ensure the move is returned within the limit.
deepseek_v4_pro/005: The strategy uses an efficient bitboard representation of the 8×8 board. All 64 possible rays (8 directions per square) are precomputed once. At each turn, the AI performs an iterative-deepening alpha‑beta search with a time budget of ~0.9 s. The evaluation function combines a standard static square‑weight table (heavily rewarding corners, penalising C‑ and X‑squares), mobility (number of legal moves), and disc difference, with weights that depend on the game phase (opening, midgame, endgame). Moves are ordered by the static value of the target square to improve pruning. If no legal move exists, the policy returns `"pass"`; otherwise it returns the best move found in algebraic notation (e.g. `"d3"`).
